Topics · One God, one message

How do I know if my inner voice is right?

Doubting your inner voice is sound. Four tests, and the Quran on a self that leans to harm and can be cleared.

Part 1 of 4

﴿وَمَآ أُبَرِّئُ نَفْسِىٓ ۚ إِنَّ ٱلنَّفْسَ لَأَمَّارَةٌۢ بِٱلسُّوٓءِ إِلَّا مَا رَحِمَ رَبِّىٓ ۚ إِنَّ رَبِّى غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil, except those upon which my Lord has mercy. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful."[601]

Translator's notes

[601] Although Ibn Katheer attributes the words of verses 52-53 to the wife of al-ʿAzeez, others have concluded that they were spoken by Joseph, thereby justifying his request for an inquiry and acknowledging Allāh's mercy to him.

Quran · Yusuf 12:53

Translation

Don’t go after your lusts. Restrain your appetites. If you give fully to your soul the delight of her desire, she will make you the laughing stock of your enemies. Don’t make merry in much luxury, and don’t be tied to its expense.

Original · Ancient Greek

Ὀπίσω τῶν ἐπιθυμιῶν σου μὴ πορεύου, καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν ὀρέξεών σου κωλύου. Ἐὰν χορηγήσεῃς τῇ ψυχῇ σου εὐδοκίαν ἐπιθυμίας, ποιήσει σε ἐπίχαρμα τῶν ἐχθρῶν σου. Μὴ εὐφραίνου ἐπὶ πολλῇ τρυφῇ, μηδὲ προσδεθῇς συμβολῇ αὐτῆς.

Sirach · 18:30-32

World English Bible

Start with the admission you just made, because it is the right one. An inner voice is not an oracle. It can be tired, frightened, flattered or hungry. The verse records a speaker, at the moment it would be easiest to claim innocence, refusing to clear their own self of blame, and saying that the self leans toward what harms unless mercy intervenes. So distrusting your inner voice is not a lack of faith. It is the honest place to begin.

A question for you

How did you find out the voice had misled you?

If you sayLater, by what it cost
ThenHindsight is the most common teacher and an expensive one. It suggests the test you need is one that works before the cost, not after.
If you saySomeone I trust saw it first
ThenThat matters. It means a second view caught what the first missed, and the next parts come back to why.
If you sayI felt a doubt at the time and went ahead anyway
ThenThen it was not one voice but two, and part of you already knew. It is worth asking which was louder, and why.

Part 2 of 4

﴿أَرَءَيْتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَـٰهَهُۥ هَوَىٰهُ أَفَأَنتَ تَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ وَكِيلًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

Have you seen the one who takes as his god his own desire? Then would you be responsible for him?

Quran · Al-Furqan 25:43

Translation

whose end is destruction, whose god is the belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who think about earthly things.

Original · Ancient Greek

ὧν τὸ τέλος ἀπώλεια, ὧν ὁ θεὸς ἡ κοιλία καὶ ἡ δόξα ἐν τῇ αἰσχύνῃ αὐτῶν, οἱ τὰ ἐπίγεια φρονοῦντες.

Philippians · 3:19

World English Bible

One way a voice goes wrong: it only ever says what you already wanted. If your inner voice never asks anything of you, never costs you, never disagrees, it is probably serving you rather than guiding you. The verse asks the question bluntly, about a person whose own desire has become the final authority. It does not ask who is bad. It asks whether you have seen it, so that you know the shape of it when it is your own.

A question for you

Which test seems most useful?

If you sayDoes it ever tell me something I do not want to hear?
ThenA good test. A voice that only flatters is easy to spot once you ask it. If it never says no to you, treat it as a mood.
If you sayDoes it still hold when it costs me?
ThenA harder test, and a fair one. Moods tend not to survive a price. What stays when it costs you is more likely to be something deeper.
If you sayWould I say it aloud to someone who loves me and would tell me the truth?
ThenThat brings in an outside view, which is the thing the first part pointed to. It is hard to talk yourself into something in front of an honest friend.

Part 3 of 4

﴿بَلِ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِۦ بَصِيرَةٌ١٤ وَلَوْ أَلْقَىٰ مَعَاذِيرَهُۥ١٥﴾

Translation of the meaning

Rather, man, against himself, will be a witness,[1804] Even if he presents his excuses.

Translator's notes

[1804] As described in 36:65 and 41:20-23.

Quran · Al-Qiyamah 75:14-15

Translation

Before judgment, examine yourself, and in the hour of scrutiny you will find forgiveness. Humble yourself before you get sick. In the time of sins, repent.

Original · Ancient Greek

Πρὸ κρίσεως ἐξέταζε σεαυτόν, καὶ ἐν ὥρᾳ ἐπισκοπῆς εὑρήσεις ἐξιλασμόν. Πρὶν ἀῤῥωστῆσαί σε ταπεινώθητι, καὶ ἐν καιρῷ ἁμαρτημάτων δεῖξον ἐπιστροφήν.

Sirach · 18:20-21

World English Bible

Under the excuses, most of us know. We can argue ourselves into almost anything, but the arguing is itself a sign: we were told something first, and now we are working to overrule it. The verse says a person has clear sight about himself even while he offers his excuses. So one test is to notice the excuse. If you are building a case, there was probably already a verdict. A true inner voice rarely needs a defence team.

A question for you

Think of one decision where you built a case. Was the case for your first instinct or against it?

If you sayFor it: I was talking myself into it
ThenThen the instinct came first and the reasons followed. That is not always wrong, but it is a signal to slow down and ask who the reasons were for.
If you sayAgainst it: I was talking myself out of it
ThenThen something in you wanted it, and something else resisted. The question is which of the two was the mood. Neither automatically is.
If you sayI cannot recall one
ThenThat is possible. Try again tomorrow, with a smaller choice. The pattern is easiest to see in small things.

Part 4 of 4

﴿وَنَفْسٍ وَمَا سَوَّىٰهَا٧ فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَىٰهَا٨ قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن زَكَّىٰهَا٩ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَن دَسَّىٰهَا١٠﴾

Translation of the meaning

And [by] the soul and He who proportioned it[1932] And inspired it [with discernment of] its wickedness and its righteousness, He has succeeded who purifies it, And he has failed who instills it [with corruption].

Translator's notes

[1932] i.e., balanced and refined it, creating in it sound tendencies and consciousness.

Quran · Ash-Shams 91:7-10

Translation

(for when Gentiles who don’t have the law do by nature the things of the law, these, not having the law, are a law to themselves, in that they show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience testifying with them, and their thoughts among themselves accusing or else excusing them)

Original · Ancient Greek

ὅταν γὰρ ἔθνη τὰ μὴ νόμον ἔχοντα φύσει τὰ τοῦ νόμου ποιῶσιν, οὗτοι νόμον μὴ ἔχοντες ἑαυτοῖς εἰσιν νόμος· οἵτινες ἐνδείκνυνται τὸ ἔργον τοῦ νόμου γραπτὸν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν, συμμαρτυρούσης αὐτῶν τῆς συνειδήσεως καὶ μεταξὺ ἀλλήλων τῶν λογισμῶν κατηγορούντων ἢ καὶ ἀπολογουμένων,

Romans · 2:14-15

World English Bible

Two tendencies, one soul. The verse says a soul was shaped, and in it were placed both its pull toward harm and its awareness of what keeps it whole. It does not leave this as a problem. It says the one who cleans the soul does well, and the one who buries it comes to loss. Cleaning is work: slow, repeated, ordinary. So the question of soul or mood is not answered once. It is a practice, and getting better at it is the hope.

A question for you

What is one ordinary thing that clears your own head?

The same in the other books

Translation

Put to death therefore your members which are on the earth: sexual immorality, uncleanness, depraved passion, evil desire, and covetousness, which is idolatry.

Original · Ancient Greek

Νεκρώσατε οὖν τὰ μέλη τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, πορνείαν, ἀκαθαρσίαν, πάθος, ἐπιθυμίαν κακήν, καὶ τὴν πλεονεξίαν ἥτις ἐστὶν εἰδωλολατρία,

Colossians · 3:5

World English Bible

Translation

He who has clean hands and a pure heart; who has not lifted up his soul to falsehood, and has not sworn deceitfully.

Original · Hebrew

נְקִ֥י כַפַּ֗יִם וּֽבַר־לֵ֫בָ֥ב אֲשֶׁ֤ר ׀ לֹא־נָשָׂ֣א לַשָּׁ֣וְא נַפְשִׁ֑י וְלֹ֖א נִשְׁבַּ֣ע לְמִרְמָֽה׃

the Psalms · 24:4

World English Bible

How then may this be attained?—Resolve, now if never before, to approve thyself to thyself; resolve to show thyself fair in God’s sight; long to be pure with thine own pure self and God!

Stoic writings · Golden Sayings 76

Epictetus, Golden Sayings (Crossley)

Translation

“Son of man, these men have taken their idols into their heart, and put the stumbling block of their iniquity before their face. Should I be inquired of at all by them?

Original · Hebrew

בֶּן־אָדָ֗ם הָאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ הֶעֱל֤וּ גִלּֽוּלֵיהֶם֙ עַל־לִבָּ֔ם וּמִכְשׁ֣וֹל עֲוֺנָ֔ם נָתְנ֖וּ נֹ֣כַח פְּנֵיהֶ֑ם הַאִדָּרֹ֥שׁ אִדָּרֵ֖שׁ לָהֶֽם׃

Ezekiel · 14:3

World English Bible
